 Phytoestrogens  
Good or bad?  
The assumption by most oncologists and pharmacists is that ALL 
phytoestrogens are bad. This is not the case.  
 
Although some are estrogenic, many have the capability to block  
estrogen from binding to the receptor proteins on the cell surface.  
 
A study by Ingram et al found that both pre - and post -menopausal 
women who consumed phytoestrogens regularly had a reduced risk of 
breast cancer.  
 
 
Phytoestrogens also have anti -angiogenic properties, inhibit tumour 
growth, act as aromatase inhibitors, and enhance the effects of 
radiotherapy treatment.  
 
The main types of anti -oestrogen acting phytoestrogens are lignans, 
isoflavones and coumestans.  
 
 
Isoflavones  
The three most common isoflavones are genistein, equol and daidzein. 
These are largely found in soy. Genistein and daidzein can be found 
in foods such as currants, fava beans, soybeans, Tofu, tempeh, and 
miso.  
 
14 
 Equol on the other hand cannot be found in food. It is produced when 
diadzein is metabolized in the intestines to create an intestinal 
bacterium. The right gut microbiome is necessary to produce equol, 
and not everyone has the ability to produce it. Seaweed consumption 
is a way to increase production of equol.  
 
When choosing soy products, it is important to select the ‘healthy’ 
options such as miso, tempeh and tofu. The processed versions of soy, 
such as soy based vegetarian products and soy milk, contain much 
higher levels of genistein and this can have the reverse effect of 
raising estrogen.  
 
Lignans  
Sesame seeds and flaxseeds are known to be two of the plant foods 
with the highest yielding content of lignans. Flaxseeds have been 
shown to bind both estrogen and testosterone in the bowel and 
eliminate it from the body. Studies show that best results come from 
ground flaxseed rather than oil or whole flaxseeds. 1 tablespoon per 
day.  
 
Coumestans : split peas, pinto beans, lima beans, alfalfa, brussels 
sprouts, spinach, and red clover; however, the later comes with a 
caution, and should only be used as advised by a health practitioner. 
See below.  
 
Red Clover  contains biochanin A. In studies this has shown to inhibit 
metabolism of the carcinogen benzo(a) pyrene, which suggests it has 
chemo preventative properties. It is an inhibitor of CYP3A4, so be 
aware of that as it can increase liver toxicity if taken with any drugs 
metabolized using the P450 liver enzyme system.   
15 
  
Resveratrol is considered safe when pre -menopausal but not post 
menopause because of its phytoestrogen properties. There is not 
enough evidence to suggest it is safe, so best to avoid.  
 
 
 
Binding ability  
The key factor of all phytoestrogens is their ability to bind to the 
receptor known as the RBA (Relative Binding Affinity).  
 
The electrical charge, size and shape determines the ability of the 
receptor to close around them, and as the majority are so weak in 
estradil, binding cannot take place.

Blood Brain Barrier.  
 
Breast Cancer can metastasise to the brain. MRI scans should be 
performed to monitor this.  
 
The blood brain barrier consists of capillary endothelial cells and a 
membrane to protect the brain from toxins, which includes 
chemotherapies and other targeted drugs. The endothelial cells are 
fused together by proteins which restrict blood components from 
crossing through the barrier.  
 
Molecules within the barrier are responsible for angiogenesis (blood 
vessel growth) and signalling.  
 
Membrane proteins within the brain are known as uptake and efflux 
transporters. Downregulation of efflux transporter proteins can also 
create a more penetrable blood brain barrier.  
 
Understanding how to break down the barrier and finding supports 
that will help drugs to be safely delivered through it, are key factors in 
treating brain metastases, very few chemotherapy drugs cross the 
blood brain barrier.  
 
The endothelial cells contain transporters such as multi -drug resistant 
proteins MDRP1 -9, ABCG2 (also known as BBRP) and P -
Glycoprotein mediated efflux.  
 
17 
 Histone protein acylation modulators can impact on MDRP -1 to 
reduce drug resistance.  
Regulators of histone proteins include green tea EGCG, curcumin, 
quercetin, grape cyanidins, L Carnitine, sulforaphane, artichoke, 
silymarin from milk Thistle, Genistein and apigenin.  
 
ABCG2 is the protein responsible from stopping drug resistance in 
breast cancer. It is also known as BCRP.  
 
BCRP can be increased by indole 3 carbinol, green tea, resveratrol 
(not in post -menopausal women), Quercetin, and fruit and vegetables 
such as apples, grapes, onions, broccoli, and cabbage.  
 
P-Glycoprotein limits the bioavailability of drugs taken orally.  
It does this by pumping them back into the lumen (membrane of the 
intestine). This promotes drug elimination into the urine and the bile 
and protects organs such as the brain, testes and lymphocytes.  
 
P-Glycoprotein has been recognised as a contributing factor to 
resistance to drugs such as vinca alkaloids, taxanes, etoposide, 
lonafarnib, imatinib and topotecan.  
 
P-Glycoprotein (P -gp) pumps cytotoxins such as chemotherapy out of 
the cells. Regulators of this are Genistein, Curcumin, Quercetin, 
Apigenin, Carnosol in Rosemary (synergistic with D3) and hypericin. 
These will help to keep drugs in the cells for longer.  
 
Inhibiting P -Glycoprotein transportation has shown to increase drug 
levels of Paclitaxel.  
 
18 
 Acetyl L Carnitine helps to carry meds and supplement through the 
BB barrier. It must be acetyl form to cross BB barrier.  
Grapeseed repairs the BB barrier to help drugs to cross.  
 
Artesunate crosses the blood/brain barrier better than Artemisinin.  
 
DMSO 400mg 4 x daily can help penetrate the BB barrier.

The Endothelial cells also contain organic anion transporters (OATS),
